reigns.note: Having accidentally killed his grandfather Acrisius, he exchanged kingdoms with Megapenthes — taking Tiryns and founding walled Mycenae with the Cyclopes.
Son of Perseus; succeeded at Mycenae and Tiryns after his father went down to Megara.
Son of Sthenelus and Nicippe; Hera's chosen lord of Mycenae, who set Heracles his labours and later perished when the Heraclids invaded the Peloponnese.
Son of Pelops; after Eurystheus' line failed he recovered the kingdom from his brother Thyestes and began the curse on the house.

reigns.citation: Hom. Il. 2.104-108; Apollod. Epit. 2.15; Hyg. Fab. 97
reigns.note: Son of Atreus, lord of many-islanded Mycenae — the sceptre Hephaestus made for Pelops passed to him, and from his citadel the Achaeans sailed against Troy.
Son of Thyestes; while Agamemnon was at Troy he seduced Clytemnestra and, on the king's return, murdered him — ruling Mycenae for seven years until Orestes came home.
Son of Agamemnon; avenged his father by killing Aegisthus and Clytemnestra, then was purified and restored to his father's throne.
